children: , the Dutch chipmaking equipment leader, won broader commitments for its roughly $400 million High-NA EUV machines. Its U.S. shares still fell about 1.8% to $1,713.41 at 10.45am ET Time on Thursday morning. The customer interest is growing; the stock's price leaves investors expecting a lot from it.
According to ASML, Intel is already using High-NA in volume production on selected chip layers. Samsung (SSNLF) plans to bring the technology into DRAM production in 2028, while TSMC

targets advanced chip production from 2030. ASML says its EXE:5200B can print features 1.7 times smaller than its current NXE systems in a single exposure. That could spare customers some costly manufacturing steps.

The price is the catch. Chipmakers need enough output and yield gains to earn back the cost of each machine, and ASML needs those gains to turn early commitments into lasting demand. At $1,713.41, the shares sit 35.5% above the roughly $1,260 GF Value estimate. That premium puts real pressure on High-NA to deliver on the factory floor.

title: ASML Drops 1.8% as $400 Million High-NA Tools Reach More Fabs
